title: S&P Global Flash US PMI (Sep 2026) — 09:45 ET, the date this survey's information actually lands
source: EST: two independent primary reads, both fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's initial research. (1) S&P Global's own PMI calendar, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 23 ... 13:45 UTC S&P Global Flash US PMI' — 13:45 UTC is 09:45 ET under EDT. (2) The 09:45 ET slot itself is corroborated by the embargo line of three consecutive S&P Global flash press releases fetched direct as PDFs (HTTP 200): 'News Release Embargoed until 0945 EDT (1345 UTC) 23 June 2026', '... 24 July 2026' and '... 21 August 2026'. Filed estimate on the standing schema gap this calendar has now hit three times, not on date doubt: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private PMI compiler (CAL: is aggregator cross-ref; this is the publisher's primary), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep.
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), reading the single prior proposal (…from-sp-global-services-pmi-2026-10-05.json) as input per EVENT-RESEARCH.md. IMPACT RAISED low -> medium ON A FIRST-HAND MEASUREMENT, and the measurement is the whole reason this entry exists. The proposing ledger filed it low and flagged the flash's own 09:45-10:00 ET window as NOT YET MEASURED. Measured here on Yahoo 5-minute bars (range=60d, delivered 2026-06-12..09-08; n=60 sessions, 50 for ^TNX), 15-minute windows percentile-ranked against their own distributions: across the three flash release days in sample (2026-06-23, 2026-07-24, 2026-08-21) the 09:45-10:00 window ran ABOVE its own median in 11 of 14 instrument-days and at or above p90 in 5 of 14 against a 10% base rate — the mirror image of the same window on the two FINAL release days, which ran below its own median in 9 of 10. The flash is the loud half of this survey and the final is the quiet half, which is exactly what the pre-announcement mechanism predicts. Not tradeable and not proposed as such: across the same three days the cross-instrument direction never resolved into a readable reaction function, and one of the three (08-21, also monthly opex) was quiet. medium here means 'this window moves and deserves a real look', never 'size it'. Same 09:45 ET slot as chicago-pmi-2026-09-30, which this calendar already carries at medium. FALSIFIER ON THE TIER ITSELF: if the 2026-09-23 window ranks below its own median in 3 or more of SPY/QQQ/TLT/IWM/^TNX, the loud finding is 1-for-2 out of sample and the tier goes back to low. Full workup and ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23.md.
